en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Eliminating All Obstacles of Lightning and Fulfilling All Wishes as Desired,
translated at the Temple of Indra’s Palace in Uḍḍiyāna, North India.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Dharma, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in a monastery in the kingdom of Śrāvastī.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"Listen attentively now; there is a dhāraṇī sūtra called 'The Fulfillment of All Wishes According to Prayer,' which eliminates all obstacles and calamities caused by lightning."
This was proclaimed by the Tathāgatas, the Unsurpassed, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past.
Just as I do now, out of constant compassion,
for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings in the heavens and among humans so that they may attain peace and happiness.
He also proclaimed it once more.
Ānanda said, "So be it, World-Honored One; I wish and desire to hear it.
The World-Honored One replied:

Ānanda, in the east there is a lightning named Agana (translated in the Song language as "Without Thickness"); in the south there is a lightning named Śatru (translated in the Song language as "Following the Current"); and in the west there is a lightning named Emitting Radiance.
In the north there is a lightning bolt named Sautanāni, which in the language of Song means "Hundred-Born Tree.
Ānanda, if there are sons or daughters of good family who know this name and title of the vidyā-mantra, [they shall be protected].
In whatever direction one dwells, there shall be no such terrors of thunder and lightning.
If such flashes of lightning should occur at one's dwelling place,
by merely writing this mantra and installing it there, all lightning will be unable to strike.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these words and phrases of the Nṛmiṇa mantra:
*tadyathā | nime nimandale | trailokya-lokajini | śūrabhāṇi | rākṣasa-rākṣasa-mām [insert name] | sarvavinayopāye | svāhā*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara...
Together with his own assembly, he gathered and sat to one side.
Then, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"World-Honored One, I too shall proclaim this True Dharma."
The mantra syllables of Nṛmiṇa are as follows: *tadyathā | vinaśapratyathariṭe | pratyathamiṭre*.
3. Mṛdī-muktike, 4. Vimali, 5. Prabhāsakare, 6.
Anna-le, 7. Bhaṇale, 8. Svahite, 9. Bhaṇaravatsini, 10. Matikārala, 11. Kapi-lambe.
Gara kṣiṇa-dimu kṣi ra-kṣa ra-kṣa-ma sva-kāra-miṭṭi-yu-paye-vīya maṃ.
16. *paśyantu* (17) *sajvālakaramṛditābala* (18) *aryavālukītiśvarādhyeṣa svāhā* (19) *iti*.
At that time, the Lord of Secrets Vajrapāṇi joined his palms in reverence toward the Buddha and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"I too shall proclaim the dhāraṇī mantra verses of this True Dharma, which are as follows:"

*Tan-ti-ya* (tadyathā) | *mu-ni mu-ni* | *mu-ni-ma-ti* | *ma-ti-su-ma-ti* | *ma-ha-ma-ti* | *ha ha ha ha* | *mā-dra-nā-siddhi-pabbaṃ* | *vajra-pāṇi-rakṣa* | *nir-ṭa svāhā*. Blessed One, this chapter is named "The Invincible."
If there are those who recollect, uphold, transcribe, or make offerings [to this],
I shall constantly protect them from all fears,
and they shall immediately attain liberation from all premature deaths.
At that time, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I too shall proclaim these dhāraṇī mantras and verses of the True Dharma."
For the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings,
he then spoke this dhāraṇī:
*Tadyathā | hiri miri ciri svāhā | mahābrahmaṇi | brahmāṅgavati | puṣpasaṃskṛte svāhā* “World-Honored One, this is called the Brahmā-dharanī of Difficult Attainment.”
It can rescue and protect all from premature death,
enabling them to attain long life,
and causing all sinful karma to be completely extinguished.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, approached the World-Honored One;
with palms joined in reverence, he addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"I too shall proclaim this dhāraṇī-mantra chapter of the True Dharma, which says:"

*Tadyathā:* *Buddhamātṛ* (1), *manini* (2), *karyandari* (3), *caṇḍālimadgī* (4), *bhukṣi* (5), *svalapate* (6), *hinamade* (7), *taraṇi* (8), *makhulini ke* (9), *cakravākī* (10), *śavari śavari svāhā* (11). O Bhagavat, this mantra-phrase of mine is named Vajrāsana.
All fears and untimely deaths shall be without obstruction, and one will attain complete liberation.
At that time, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka, the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, and the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa—
Joining their palms toward the Buddha, they addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One, we Four Great Kings shall also proclaim these words and phrases of the dhāraṇī of this True Dharma, which are as follows:

*Tadyathā:* *1. Puṣpe* *2. Supuṣpe* *3. Durdharṣe* *4. Āryaprasādite* *5. Śāntini mudite* *6. Kumbhīre* *7. Kṣaṇikābhyudgate* *8. Sthūlanāsasatavinite svāhā.* World-Honored One, these mantra-words spoken by us Four Kings are called 'Fearlessness' (*Abhaya*)."
They shall provide protection against all fears and ensure that the lives of all beings do not meet with untimely death.
At that time, there were the Naga King Sagara, the Naga King Manasvī, the Naga King Vidyutprabha, and the Naga King Anavatapta.
The Nāga King Vidyujjihva, the Nāga King Śataraśmi, and others likewise stood to one side before the World-Honored One with palms joined in reverence.
The World-Honored One addressed them, saying: "Wherever these verses of the wish-fulfilling mantra exist..."
It protects against all obstacles caused by lightning;
it is also able to rescue and protect those who die prematurely, eliminate all poisons,
and [ward off] all *kakkana-veṭṭhana*.
Those who perform inauspicious deeds shall also be utterly destroyed.
Listen attentively, you must give rise to a heart of compassion.
Within your realm of the nāga destiny, [you must act accordingly].
"Each of you should subdue the anger, pride, and arrogance that arise within you.
The nāgas asked, "How should we subdue them?
The World-Honored One replied, "I possess a dhāraṇī."
This shall cause the pride and arrogance of you nāgas to be immediately stilled.
The mantra is as follows:

Tadyathā: (1) ājale, (2) mamale, (3) amṛte, (4) akṣaye, (5) avyaye, (6) bhaṇiyaparyaye, (7) sarvabhadre, (8) praśamani svāhā, (9) arthabhañja, (10) saubhāgye svāhā, (11) indraśāne svāhā, (12) maheśāne svāhā. The World-Honored One spoke thus.
If there are men or women who receive,
uphold, read, recite, transcribe, and make offerings to these mantra verses and phrases.
Those nāgas, devas, lightning, and other such terrors cannot cause them harm.
Furthermore, there are no poisons from roots or compounded poisons;
all man-made poisons are likewise unable to harm us or any sentient beings.
At that time, Mahābrahmā, Śakra, the Lord of Devas,
the Four World-Protecting Kings, the various Dragon Kings,
and others exclaimed in praise: "Excellent, excellent, O Worthy One!"
For the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to the great multitude of sentient beings,
we shall single-mindedly receive and uphold these well-spoken mantra verses of the *Dharmadhātu-nirmāṇa*.
When the Buddha had spoken this sutra,
all the world— including devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and the great assembly—
having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for the Elimination of All Lightning and the Fulfillment of Every Wish According to One's Desires.
